title: 2019: After the Fall of New York

facts.text: Director Sergio Martino and screenwriter Ernesto Gastaldi are credited under fake American names: "Martin Dolman" and "Julian Barry". Italian exploitation films loved a Hollywood-sounding alias.
Director Sergio Martino is best known for giallo thrillers. A post-apocalyptic action movie was a big swerve for him.
Released in the U.S. in 1984, this film was first rated X for extreme violence. It was trimmed to earn an R rating.
Most of the film was shot at De Paolis Studios in Rome. The desert scenes were filmed in Arizona, with some exteriors shot in New York City.
Richard Scheib of Moria called this "one of the more enjoyable Italian Mad Max ripoffs" but gave it only two stars out of five.
The guns carried by the white-suited government guards look just like the weapon Jane Fonda used in Barbarella (1968), which even appeared on that film's posters.
Edmund Purdom, who plays the Confederacy's President, didn't provide his own voice here: he was dubbed by another actor.
Romano Puppo (Ratchet) was primarily a stuntman before acting. He later turned up in Orca (1977) and Escape from the Bronx (1983).
An IMDb goof: in a wide shot of the heroes riding motorcycles toward New York, Ratchet is obviously a stunt double, though actor Romano Puppo was a veteran stuntman himself.
The skyline of ruined Manhattan relied on art tricks. Anna Kanakis (Ania) recalls a matte painting of the Twin Towers, per Mondo Digital's review of the Blu-ray interviews.
The synth score is by Guido and Maurizio De Angelis, billed as "Oliver Onions". It has reportedly never had an official soundtrack release.
Paolo Maria Scalondro, who plays Bronx, got a Blu-ray featurette called "Hook Man". He talks about acting with a hook hand, convincingly gouging eyes, and using his motorcycle skills on set.
Look closely at the "sewer rats" devouring a victim: in a close-up, the rat chewing on flesh is clearly a guinea pig.
Valentine Monnier (Giara) was a model first. She appeared on the September 1977 cover of Cosmopolitan before later leaving acting to become a photographer.
Production designer Antonello Geleng says he aimed for a "metaphysic abstraction" for the sets, blending futuristic elements with the medieval past, per Mondo Digital's Blu-ray review.
Picasso's Guernica hangs in the background here. Alfonso Cuarón's Children of Men (2006) also stages a scene before Guernica, and also has a world without fertile women.
Anna Kanakis (Ania) was crowned Miss Italia 1977, then disqualified from Miss World that year when it emerged she was only 15.
Cinematographer Giancarlo Ferrando also shot director Sergio Martino's giallo Torso. The No-Budget Nightmares podcast credits Martino's giallo background for this film's colorful look.
Wikipedia says the film was heavily influenced by John Carpenter's Escape from New York and George Miller's Mad Max 2, and belongs to the same Italian wave as 1990: The Bronx Warriors.
This Italian knock-off has a long afterlife: IMDb's connections list shows it referenced in Man of Steel (2013) and Ready Player One (2018), as well as Children of Men (2006).
Star Michael Sopkiw was cast after modeling work. Lamberto Bava (son of Mario Bava) then directed him in Blastfighter (1984), and he made just four films before retiring.
This was director Sergio Martino's first post-nuke film. He returned to the wasteland three years later with Hands of Steel (1986), per Mondo Digital.
Anna Kanakis says she memorized all her English dialogue phonetically on a chaotic, multilingual set, according to a Blu-ray interview described by Mondo Digital.
IMDb's connections list shows this film referencing Planet of the Apes (1968), Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid (1969), Escape from New York (1981), Yor (1983) and 2020 Texas Gladiators (1983).
George Eastman, who plays Big Ape, has spoken fondly of the film. In a Blu-ray interview he calls director Sergio Martino "distant" on set, according to Mondo Digital.
In the early 1990s, retired star Michael Sopkiw walked into a California video store. The clerk, a huge fan of this film, was Quentin Tarantino.
The 2003 Media Blasters DVD was recalled and reissued without its audio commentary, reportedly because of verbal barbs in the track, says Mondo Digital.
In this shot of the heroes panning to Shorty, a crew member can be seen moving behind part of the car at the edge of the frame.
Michael Sopkiw says he didn't expect to be dubbed, and that a dispute with the Screen Actors Guild cost him his membership, per Mondo Digital's review of the Blu-ray commentary.
In a Blu-ray interview, director Sergio Martino says Italian studios failed to adopt new visual effects in the late 1980s and early 90s. He says that hurt Italian sci-fi and fantasy, per DVD Talk.
An IMDb continuity goof: when George Eastman's Big Ape hurls his scimitar at the Eurac soldiers, the blade spins clockwise, then counter-clockwise by the time it decapitates them.
The quest for the last fertile human later resurfaced in Hell Comes to Frogtown, American Cyborg: Steel Warrior and Children of Men, notes Richard Scheib of Moria.
Germany cut the film to win an FSK-18 rating, yet it was still BPjM-indexed until 2009. The uncut version only got an FSK-16 rating in 2016.
In the US, Almi Pictures gave it a theatrical release on December 7, 1984, per Reel Reviews. Vestron later put it out on VHS, per Mondo Digital.
TV Guide gave it one star out of five, calling it "silly at best" with "bad acting, and laughable special effects."
Code Red's 2017 Blu-ray used a new HD scan of the English version, because the cast spoke English on set. The film was shot MOS-style multilingual, then dubbed.
